verdict.rationale: Postman's own mock servers let you simulate API behavior for testing and development, including local mock servers for simulations, so tests can run against a stand-in instead of the real API. Environments are listed as a feature but are not documented here as separating sandbox from production. Nothing shows agent-driven work (Agent Mode, CLI-for-agents) being confined to mocks or isolated from production data. missing for 10: documented isolation guarantees keeping production data untouched, evidence that agent-driven requests can be scoped or restricted to a sandbox or mock target, documented environment separation for sandbox vs. production, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Start mock servers to simulate API behavior for testing and development.
Create a mock server in Postman to simulate a real API server that’s always available to handle requests.
Run simulations against local mock servers to test how your service responds to disruptions and performance constraints.
